annotation.title_clean: Position Paper (China) — CCW/GGE.1/2018/WP.7, Group of Governmental Experts on Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems
annotation.title_en: Position Paper submitted by China to the CCW Group of Governmental Experts on LAWS (CCW/GGE.1/2018/WP.7)
annotation.authors_or_issuer: People's Republic of China (submitted to the CCW Group of Governmental Experts)
annotation.venue: UN Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons, Group of Governmental Experts, Geneva
annotation.summary_en: This is China's April 2018 position paper to the CCW Group of Governmental Experts on lethal autonomous weapons systems (LAWS). It proposes defining LAWS as fully autonomous by five characteristics and asks for clarity on human-machine interaction. It finds that applying humanitarian law to LAWS is uncertain, urges restraint in their use, warns against prejudging AI development, and doubts that national weapon reviews are enough.
key_provisions_or_claims: Defines LAWS by five characteristics: lethality, autonomy, impossibility of termination, indiscriminate effect, and evolution.
Says meaningful human control and human judgment need further clarification on the mode and degree of human involvement.
Calls on all states to exercise precaution and refrain from indiscriminate use of LAWS against civilians, pending a solution.
Holds that LAWS should be subject to humanitarian law (distinction, proportionality, precaution) but notes doubts about applying it and about establishing accountability.
Warns against preset premises that could impede AI development, and argues national weapon reviews cannot fundamentally resolve LAWS concerns.
